output.stageDescription: Bar Raiser — leadership-principle walkthrough grounded in real project evidence, with honesty calibration per story.
output.coachingNotes: Walk each principle from your own evidence; calibrate every story honestly and frame gaps without fabricating.

barRaiserWalkthrough.interpretation: You act on behalf of the whole, not just your task; evidence of owning an outcome end-to-end, including the parts nobody assigned you.

stories.title: Owned the EKS migration end-to-end
stories.situation: Our deploys took 40 minutes and required a manual cutover step that blocked releases.
stories.task: I decided to migrate the workload to EKS with an automated cutover.
stories.action: I designed the migration, built the controller, and ran the dual-read window myself.
stories.result: Deploy time dropped from 40 minutes to under 8 minutes and the manual step was removed.
stories.honestyCalibration: This was solo work. Frame as 'I designed and drove the migration', NOT 'I led a team through it'. If asked who else was involved, say plainly that you owned it end-to-end — that is a strong ownership signal on its own. The under-8-minutes figure is measured from CI logs, so it holds up.
stories.seniorityNote: Owning an infra migration end-to-end reads as senior IC. Do not stretch it into 'I set the org's migration strategy' — the evidence is one project, not a mandate.

probingQuestions.question: Who else worked on this, and what specifically was yours?
probingQuestions.framing: I owned it end-to-end — design, the controller, and the cutover. There was no team; that is the honest answer and it is still a strong ownership story.

barRaiserWalkthrough.interpretation: You raise the performance bar with every hire and actively grow other engineers.

probingQuestions.question: Tell me about someone you developed.
probingQuestions.framing: I haven't held that responsibility yet — my work has been solo/IC. I can describe how I'd approach it and point to the docs others rely on as the closest real signal.

barRaiserWalkthrough.gapGuidance: Your projects show no evidence of hiring, mentoring, or growing other engineers yet — expected for solo/IC work. Be honest in the room: say you haven't held that responsibility, then describe how you'd approach it and bridge from the nearest real signal. Never fabricate a mentee or a hiring loop.
